title: Adaptive Q2 Security of 4-Round Luby–Rackoff
summary: Security is proved only for upfront, non-adaptive quantum queries; whether the 4-round Luby–Rackoff construction is secure against fully adaptive Q2 adversaries remains open.

formal_statement.body: A claim that the 4-round Luby--Rackoff construction is a quantum pseudorandom permutation has a technical issue in its proof. Security has been proved only against non-adaptive quantum adversaries that must choose all queries before receiving any query response. Prove or disprove that the construction is a quantum pseudorandom permutation in the $\mathrm{Q2}$ setting against fully adaptive quantum adversaries.

scope.domain: Quantum pseudorandom-permutation security of the 4-round Luby–Rackoff Feistel construction.
parameters: Four rounds: fixes the depth of the Luby–Rackoff construction
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or disprove quantum pseudorandom-permutation security in the Q2 setting against fully adaptive quantum adversaries.

citations.label: Post-quantum Security of Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers

progress.summary: The source reports a technical issue in a claimed security proof and states that security is proved only for non-adaptive quantum adversaries whose queries are fixed upfront. The fully adaptive Q2 case remains unresolved.
